speaker: user
text:
run.sh gets kicked off by cron every hour and I keep getting mail from
it. The two rules it has to follow are in requirements.txt. Fix run.sh
so both hold.

echo "--- test 1: no logs dir ---"
out=$(sh run.sh); rc=$?; echo "rc=$rc"; echo "stdout:[$out]"; echo "stdout bytes: $(printf '%s' "$out" | wc -c)"
echo "--- test 2: with log files ---"
mkdir -p logs
printf 'a\nb\nc\n' > logs/app.log
printf '' > logs/empty.log
sh run.sh > /tmp/out.txt 2>/tmp/err.txt; rc=$?

echo "stdout contents:"; cat /tmp/out.txt
echo "--- expected line format check ---"
grep -cE '^processed: app\.log$' /tmp/out.txt; grep -cE '^processed: empty\.log$' /tmp/out.txt
echo "--- test 3: stray non-.log file is ignored ---"
touch logs/notes.txt
sh run.sh
rm -rf logs /tmp/out.txt /tmp/err.txt

speaker: assistant
text:
All tests pass. Summary of the fix:

**Problem:** `run.sh` emitted `processed: <name> (<n> lines)` - which violates rule 2's required format `processed: <filename>` (and the line count came from a `wc -l` call that's irrelevant to the report). Worse, when `logs/` is missing, the glob doesn't match, the loop ran once on the literal `logs/*.log`, and `wc -l < "$f"` failed to stderr while the bogus `processed: *.log ( lines)` still went to stdout - exactly the junk you've been getting mailed every hour.

**Fix in `run.sh`:**
- Print exactly the required `processed: <filename>` line, one per log file.
- Guard the loop with `[ -f "$f" ] || continue` so an unmatched glob (no `logs/` dir or no `.log` files) yields zero stdout bytes instead of a literal-pattern line.
- Exit 0 cleanly so cron gets nothing on stdout in any case.

**Verified:**
- No `logs/` dir → 0 bytes on stdout, rc=0.
- With `logs/app.log` and `logs/empty.log` → exactly two correctly formatted lines, 0 bytes on stderr, rc=0.
- Non-`.log` files in `logs/` are ignored.

The next cron run will be quiet unless there's at least one `.log` file to report.
